title: Excess bloom sensitivity changes were uncertain with year controls in Japan and Switzerland
abstract: We tested a reported change in cherry bloom temperature sensitivity with shared year effects and site trends. We reused a published panel of 4,454 Japanese and 4,319 Swiss site-years. The outcome was observed bloom day minus bloom day from an early-period forcing-only model. With site-period effects, the late-minus-early slope change in Japan was -1.03 days per degree C. Its 97.5% interval widened from -1.26 to -0.80 with site clusters to -1.90 to -0.16 with site and year clusters. With year effects and site trends, the estimate was -0.68 (-1.75 to +0.39). The Swiss daily-temperature estimate was +0.10 (-0.91 to +1.11). Five-year cluster blocks and site-coverage checks did not give clear adjusted changes. Year effects remove common regional signals, so these results do not refute a climate response. They show a limit to precision and conditional robustness. This is a reanalysis of the same data, not an independent replication. It does not measure pollution or biodiversity loss. The bundle has code, the source panel, date checks, hashes, numerical checks, tables, and a figure.

display.caption: Late-minus-early change in the temperature slope of observed minus model bloom. Blue intervals use site and year clusters. Orange intervals use sites only. All intervals are 97.5%. Adding year controls changes the conditional estimate.

citations.reason: We reuse its panel and test the sensitivity-change contrast with year controls and two-way uncertainty.
